tags.name: Profile
tags.description: The account a credential belongs to.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: The API token a request carries. Tokens are created, rolled and revoked in Settings › API tokens.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: The phones that record locations (Overland installs), with their latest position and battery.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description: Where the devices have been: every point as it arrived, the places they stayed at (visits) and the all-time heatmap. All of it needs `locations:read`.

tags.name: Tracks
tags.description: Where the devices went, at a level of calculation: as recorded, averaged, mapped onto roads and railways, or as stops and moves.

tags.name: Timeline
tags.description: Stops and moves with their transport modes, the corrections people make to the modes, and distance and time per mode.

tags.name: History
tags.description: History without coordinates: trips, daily statistics and recent activity (`history:read`).

tags.name: Insights
tags.description: How you travelled: distance, time and moves per transport mode, when you travel and on which roads — worked out from the stops and moves, without coordinates (`history:read`).

tags.name: People
tags.description: The people who share their location with you, with their devices at the precision they chose.

tags.name: Sharing
tags.description: Your location shared with people (one way, for as long as you choose) and as public links, and the shares people give you.

tags.name: Access log
tags.description: Who read or changed your data — you, your tokens, the people you share with and the visitors of your links — when, through which channel and what (`audit:read`).

get.description:
The account the token or session belongs to. Its time zone decides where the account's local days begin and end.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `profile:read`, or a signed-in session.

Checks the API token the request carries and describes it: its name, scopes, devices and expiry. A token that is refused gets the usual 401 instead, so this is the call to test a token with, or to find out when it expires. Only a token can be verified: a signed-in session gets 400.

**Access:** any API token, whatever its scopes; not a session.

patch.description:
Renames the device, switches its silence alerts or queues a settings preset for Overland. A preset is for a device that records with Overland only: for another app the answer is 409. Its credentials and its app are out of reach: no token can replace a device's access token, move it to another app or delete it, which takes a signed-in session. The answer has the device and its settings after the change; the device's position only for a credential with `locations:read`.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `devices:write`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
The points one device recorded, exactly as the phone sent them (no smoothing, no map matching), oldest first and a page at a time: follow `nextCursor` until it is null. `from` and `to` narrow the range. A phone uploads when it can, so points may arrive later than newer ones: to keep a copy current, ask again for a range that overlaps the end of the last one.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
The tracks of the devices in `[from, to)` (at most 93 days) at a level of calculation: `raw` as recorded, `averaged` (outliers dropped, GPS noise smoothed), `mapped` (snapped to roads and railways, with the way's shape between points) or `inferred` (the stops and moves of the timeline, each move with its transport mode). A point that has not reached the level yet is served at the best one below it, and `availableLevel` says which level every point reached. Each device's track is simplified to at most `maxPoints`.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
The timeline: the stops and moves overlapping `[from, to)` (at most 93 days), oldest first, a page at a time. A stop has its place (`centroid`) and duration; a move its transport mode — the one a person set, else the inferred one — with the confidence, distance, duration and speeds. `pending` is true while points of the range still wait for processing, so the timeline may still change.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

put.description:
Corrects the transport mode of a move: the mode applies to the move's time and wins over the inference, also when the history is processed again. The inferred mode stays visible as `modeInferred`. Setting the mode it already has changes nothing. A stop has no mode: `409`.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `locations:read` and `locations:write`, or a signed-in session.

schema.description: The segment's id. It stays the same while the segment keeps its start.

parameters.description: The segment's id. It stays the same while the segment keeps its start.

delete.description:
Withdraws the correction that set the move's mode — a mode set from a moment on with it, for every move it covered — so the inferred mode counts again. The segment answers with the inferred mode at once; the span is worked out again within seconds (a `segments` event follows). Without a correction nothing changes.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `locations:read` and `locations:write`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
How the device travels now: the mode set from a moment on that is still in force (`override`), and the current mode — that one, or the latest segment's while it is recent (a stop is `stationary`). `current` is null when the device has not reported for a while.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

post.summary: Set the mode from now on
post.description:
The quick toggle: from now on the device travels by `mode`, until `until` or the next detected stop, whichever comes first. It is idempotent — the same mode again changes nothing — another mode ends the running one and starts anew, and `mode: null` ends it, so inference takes over again.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `locations:read` and `locations:write`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
Per local day (the account's time zone) from `from` to `to` (inclusive, at most 400 days), device and transport mode: the distance, the time and the number of segments, and how many of those a person set. Stops count as `stationary`; a segment across midnight counts on both days in proportion to its time.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `history:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
Totals of a period of local days (the account's time zone; at most three years, the whole history up to today by default) — distance, time on the move, moves, stops and active days — with the same totals for the period of as many days just before, every transport mode's distance, time, moves, average speed and share with its change since that period, and a series per day, week or month (by the period's length: up to 31 days by day, up to 26 weeks by week, else by month) of distance and time per mode. A move across the period's edge counts with the part inside it, in proportion to its time, and so across midnight and the steps of the series; counts are of the moves and stops that started inside. `pending` is true while recorded points of the period still wait for processing.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `history:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.summary: Get how you travelled in one mode
get.description:
One transport mode in a period of local days (as for the overview): distance, time, moves, average and typical speed, the longest and the fastest move; a series per day, week or month; distance and time per hour of the day and per day of the week; the distance by kind of way (from the map matching, where there was map data); for trains, trams and metros the part on railway track and the halts at stations, for boats the part on ferry routes; the moves by their median speed; and the five longest, fastest and most recent moves — segment ids and times, never where they went. An unknown mode is a 404.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `history:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
The people who share their location with you, by name, each with the devices they share and where those are, at the precision of the share: approximate and area shares give the centre of a cell around the position, never the position itself. A device's `location` is the newest position inside the share's window (its history, or the last 12 hours for live-only shares); battery and activity appear only when the share includes details. People you hid are left out. `distanceM` starts from your own most recently located device and needs `locations:read` too. Each person listed can see in their data access log that, and when, you looked.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `people:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
The people you share your location with: current shares (not stopped, not ended), newest first, with what each shows and until when, whether the address has an account yet (`pending`), whether someone signed up with it and waits for your confirmation (`joined`), whether the person hid you (`hidden`), and when they last looked.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `shares:read`, or a signed-in session.

shares.description: Current shares (not stopped, not ended), newest first.

post.description:
Starts sharing your location with a person, one way: they see you under People, you do not see them unless they share back. Pick the devices (all by default, also later ones), the precision, history (precise only; live only by default), whether battery and activity come along (yes by default) and the duration. An address without an account gets a `pending` share: when someone signs up with it, it starts at once only if they came with an invitation to that very address; otherwise it is `joined` and waits until you confirm them. The answer shows whether the address has an account, and its name. One current share per address: change it instead (409). At most 50 at a time (409). A token limited to some devices shares only those, listed by id. Needs `locations:read` as well as `shares:write`: what you share can be precise positions.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `shares:write` and `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

patch.description:
Changes what a current share shows or how long it runs: a `duration` counts from now (extend or shorten), the other fields change only when given. History stays limited to precise shares (400 otherwise). The recipient sees the change at once. A token limited to some devices changes only shares that show nothing but its devices, before and after the change (403). Needs `locations:read` as well as `shares:write`.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `shares:write` and `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

schema.description: The share's id.

parameters.description: The share's id.

delete.description:
Stops a share at once: from this moment the person sees nothing of you, in any read or live event. A pending share is withdrawn before anyone could see it.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `shares:write`, or a signed-in session.

parameters.name: id

schema.description: The share's id.

parameters.description: The share's id.

post.description:
Someone signed up with the address of a share that waited for it (`joined`): confirm that they are the person you meant, and the share starts. Trail does not verify addresses, so it does not start on its own — unless they signed up with an invitation to that very address. 409 when nobody has signed up with the address yet, or when the share already reaches its person. A token limited to some devices confirms only shares that show nothing but its devices (403).

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `shares:write` and `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

get.description:
Your public links that were not turned off — the working ones, then expired ones (kept for 30 days), each newest first, at most 50 — with what each shows, when it expires and how often it was opened. Secrets are never listed: a link's address is shown once, when it is made.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `shares:read`, or a signed-in session.

links.description: Links that were not turned off: the working ones, then expired ones, each newest first, at most 50.

post.description:
Makes a secret web address that shows your location to anyone who has it, without an account: a page with the label, the devices you pick at the precision you pick, optionally their track of the last days (precise only) and battery and activity. Without a label it reads “Shared location”, never your name. It always expires — in 24 hours unless you choose another time, at least an hour and at most 30 days away — and you can turn it off at any time. The answer carries the secret and the address once; Trail keeps only a hash. At most 20 links work at a time (409). Needs `locations:read` as well as `shares:write`: the link can show precise positions.

**Access:** an API token with the scopes `shares:write` and `locations:read`, or a signed-in session.

secret.description: The link's secret, shown this once.

url.description: The page to send: `<server>/s#<secret>`, shown this once. The secret is the fragment, which browsers never send to a server.

**Access:** an API token with the scope `shares:write`, or a signed-in session.

With `actorId`, all of it for one actor: what one person looked at, what one token did, how often one link was opened.

200.description: Who looked at your data, over a period.

get.description:
Who read or changed your data, a line per hour and kind of access, newest first: you in your browser, your API tokens (directly or through the MCP server), the people you share with — when they looked at you, through which share, and what — and the visitors of your public links, as their network and kind of browser. Each line says what was read or changed (devices, a range, a level, a share …), never where. Filter by period, kinds of actor, channels, action or one actor (`actorId`: a person, a token, a link or one of your browsers); follow `nextCursor` for older lines. The log is yours alone: nobody else, an administrator neither, can read it. Reading it is not recorded.

bearer.description:
An API token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer trlk_…`. Its scopes decide what it may do; an operation lists the scopes that grant access to it.

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `profile:read` | Read the account's name and time zone. |
| `devices:read` | List the devices with their name, status, last-seen time and battery, not where they are. |
| `devices:write` | Rename devices, switch their alerts and queue settings presets; never their tokens. |
| `locations:read` | Read positions: where the devices are now and where they have been (points, visits, the heatmap, tracks, the timeline). |
| `locations:write` | Correct how you travelled (transport mode overrides). |
| `history:read` | Read trips, daily statistics, activity and insights: the history without coordinates. |
| `people:read` | See the people who share their location with you. |
| `shares:read` | List your shares, the ones you receive and your public links. |
| `shares:write` | Start and stop sharing, hide people and manage public links. |
| `audit:read` | Read the data access log: who looked at or changed your data, when, how and which data — without positions. |
